 J U D G M E N T

The Police Sub-Inspector, Byatarayanapura PS submitted charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 306 of IPC.
2.

The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The deceased-Smt.Rathnamma is the sister of the complainant.
The deceased-Smt.Rathnamma and Mallikarjuna are the wife and husband.

The marriage Byatarayanapura P.S vs Mallikarjuna on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11810785/
1 of deceased and accused was performed 18 years back before elders.

After marriage,
they were having two children by name Tanuja aged 16 years and Rajesha aged 11 years, both were studying.

They came to Bengaluru 4-5 years back and staying in 3rd Main road, 2nd cross, Kasturiba Nagara and deceased was working in Medical Factory and accused was selling vegetables on push cart, the accused was consuming alcohol after marriage and used to quarrel with the deceased for silly reasons and doubting her, if she talks with others and harassed her physically and mentally.
The accused taken away the ear-rings of the deceased and returned in intoxicated condition and beaten her and thereby tortured physically and mentally.

Such being the case, on 15.08.2015, the accused returned at 7.00 p.m. being in intoxicated condition picked up quarrel for the reason C.W.7 Shivanna advised him and as the brother of the deceased i.e. complainant Shankaregowda brought the TV stand to the deceased and thereafter started to fight with the deceased and demanded her for money to consume alcohol.
When the deceased not gave the money to consume alcohol, the accused poured kerosene on her and started to harass.
As the deceased fed up with the continuous physical and mental torture, hence the deceased set ablaze herself.
She was admitted to Victoria hospital on 15.08.2015, but due to the severe burnt injuries she died on 17.08.2015 at 4.00 p.m and thereby the accused has committed the offences alleged against him.

3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned Judicial Magistrate,
Bangalore.

The learned Magistrate, after taking cognizance of the offences against the accused,
committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Section 207 of CrPC by furnishing copy of the charge sheet to the accused.

After committal, the said case was numbered as SC No.282/2016.
4.
The charge was framed against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 306 of IPC.
The accused has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5. The prosecution has examined ten witnesses as PWs.1 to 10 and got marked documents at EX.P1 to P12 and M.Os.1 to 4.
On consent of accused counsel, inquest Mahazar and postmortem report of the deceased Rathnamma have been marked at EX.P5 and 6.
As such learned PP has gave up the witnesses CW2 to 4, 17 and 18.
This court has issued summons, warrant and proclamation against the witnesses CWS.6, 8 to 10, 13 to 15.
Inspite of that the concerned police unable to execute the warrant against the said witnesses and got them present before the court for the purpose of recording of evidence.
As such the prayer of the learned PP was rejected and the witnesses CWS.6, 8 to 10, 13 to 15 were dropped.
6. After completion of prosecution side evidence, this court has recorded the statement of accused as provided under Section 313 of CrPC.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him and not opted to lead defence evidence nor submitted anything to the court.
The accused has complied Section 437A of CrPC.

7. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.

2 8.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused and deceased got married 15 years back and having one male ane one female children and residing in the house of C.W.9 No.65/5, 2nd coss, 3rd main, Kasturiba Nagar, Bengaluru, later accused consuming alcohol used to quarrel with deceased and doubting her fidelity and assaulted her and subjected the deceased to physical and mental cruelty and thereby accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.498A of Indian Penal Code, 1860?

2. Whether the prosecution proves that on 15.08.2015 at 7.00 p.m accused consuming alcohol, quarreled with deceased and assaulted her and instigating her to go and die and poured kerosene on her, due to which deceased being fed up and unable to tolerate such harassment of accused, the deceased ablaze herself and committed suicide and thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable u/s 306 of IPC?
3. What order?
9.

This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3:
As per final order  for the following:
R E A S O N S 10.
Points No.1 and 2: Both these points are taken up together for discussions as they are related with each other and to avoid repetition.

To establish due to the physical and mental harassment of the accused towards deceased and as the accused instigated the deceased to die so that he will lead happy and peaceful life, hence the deceased has committed suicide has to be proved by the prosecution.

Even though the inquest Mahazar and P.M.Report have been marked at Ex.P.5 and 6 on the consent of the accused counsel,
but as already discussed above, the burden is upon the prosecution to prove the allegations made against the accused.

In order to prove the allegations made against the accused, the prosecution has examined brother, sister and elder brother of the deceased by name Shankaregowda, Parvathamma and Shivanna as PWs.1 to 3 respectively.
The both brothers and sister of the deceased have specifically given evidence that the accused is their uncle and deceased Rathnamma is their sister.
The accused and deceased got married 15 years back and having one male and one female children and residing in the house of C.W.9 No.65/5, 2nd coss, 3rd main, Kasturiba Nagar, Bengaluru.

Byatarayanapura P.S vs Mallikarjuna on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11810785/
3
According to PWs.1 to 3, the accused never harassed the deceased either physically or mentally and they do not know the reasons for committing of suicide by their sister.
According to P.W.2 - due to stove burst, the deceased has sustained burnt injuries.
When they come to the spot after receiving the information about the incident, at that time the police have obtained their signatures on documents.
Except that they did not know anything about the contents of the complaint, their statement and panchanama.
Hence the learned PP has treated these witnesses PWs.1 to 3 as hostile and cross-examined.
Inspite of that, the learned PP failed to get any useful evidence to believe the allegations made against the accused are true.
Hence the evidence given by PWs.1 to 3 not at all in favour of the prosecution and as such same cannot be considered.
11. The witnesses P.W.4 and 5 who are the relatives of deceased and C.W.1 have also deposed almost same as above.

The accused and deceased got married 15 years back and having one male and one female children and residing in the house of C.W.9 No.65/5, 2nd coss, 3rd Main, Kasturiba Nagar,
Bengaluru.
According to PWs.4 and 5, the accused never harassed the deceased either physically or mentally and they do not know the exact reasons for committing of suicide by the deceased.
Except that they did not know anything about the contents of the complaint, their statement and panchanama.
Hence the learned PP has treated these witnesses PWs.4 and 5 as hostile and cross- examined.
Inspite of that, the learned PP failed to get any useful evidence to believe the allegations made against the accused are true.
Hence the evidence given by PWs.4 and 5 not at all in favour of the prosecution and as such same cannot be considered.
The statement of the deceased was recorded at hospital, when she was taking treatment for the burnt injuries.
According to the police records, the statement of the deceased was recorded in the presence of the Medical Officer, who has treated the deceased.
According to the evidence of Medical Officer Smt.Varalakshmi examined as P.W.6, the witness was in fit condition to give statement.

The portion of the statement i.e.
endorsement of P.W.6 present on Ex.P.3 has been marked at Ex.P.3(b) and the signature of the said Medical Officer has been marked at Ex.P.3(c).
The said statement has been recorded by one Mr.Devaraju, who is examined as P.W.9.

In the cross-examination, P.W.6 has admitted that the deceased has suffered 89% of burnt injuries and they have given seductive drugs, perhaps denied due to seductive drugs given to the deceased, she was in unconscious condition and could not give her statement.

Further denied that even though deceased was not in a position to give statement,
they have endorsed on Ex.P.3.
Such being the case, the family members and other independent witnesses not at all supported the story of prosecution.
So there is no nexus between the evidence of P.W.6 and other vital witnesses of the prosecution.

12. The evidence of said Devaraju shows that on 16.08.2015 as per the instructions of C.W.22, he went to the Victoria hospital at 4.00 p.m and after obtaining the permission of P.W.6 i.e. Medical Officer has recorded statement of the deceased and obtained her LTM, since she was not able to sign due to the burnt injuries.
According to this witness P.W.9 he read over the contents of her statement and thereafter obtained her LTM.
On 17.08.2015 the said Rathnamma succumbed in the hospital.
On 18.08.2015 he was deputed to present at the time of conducting inquest Mahazar and P.M.
The inquest Mahazar was conducted by C.W.21 and thereafter PM was carried out by C.W.18.
After completion of the P.M.Report, the dead body was handed over to him and in return he has handed over to the complainant i.e. brother of the deceased and obtained acknowledgement.
The evidence given by the said witness has completely denied by the counsel for accused.

4 cross-examination the said witness admitted that the injured was suffering about 80% of the burnt injuries and again he changed his version and said he was not aware the percentage of the burnt injuries.

sentences.text: He has denied that the deceased was not in a position to give statement.
The said witness also admitted he has not endorsed on Ex.P.3 about the starting and completion time of recording of the statement of the injured.

13. There is no specific evidence placed by the prosecution to believe whether the said deceased was in fit condition and good state of mind to give evidence since the percentage of the burnt injury was 80% as per the admission of the police witness P.W.9.

Such being the case, generally the doctors provide sedative drugs to avoid the pain to the injured persons, which generally influence the injured not to be in good state of mind or in not complete conscious condition.
Under such circumstances, the injured may be not in complete conscious condition.

Moreover the brother of the deceased Shankaregowda during his cross- examination itself though admitted his signature present on Ex.P.3, but his further evidence reveals that the police have obtained his signatures when he was outside the hospital.
According to him, her sister never gave statement that due to the harassment by accused, she committed suicide.
As such the evidence given by the complainant contrary and against to the statement prepared by the police official witness P.W.9 Mr.Devaraju.

14. It is necessary to note that the witness P.W.7 Lakshman.C shows that on 18.08.2015 he went to the mortuary of Victoria hospital alongwith C.W.19 and conducted inquest Mahazar and recorded statement of CWs.2 to 7.
After completion of the inquest Mahazar on the dead body, he has submitted requisition to C.W.18 to conduct PM on the dead body of the deceased.
After completion of the P.M handed over the dead body to its relative and obtained endorsement and thereafter handed over further investigation to the C.W.22/P.W.8 i.e. Krishnamurthy.
The said evidence has completely denied by the accused counsel.
15. The another witness P.W.10 Venkateshaiah being the ASI deposed that on 15.08.2015 when he was SHO the complainant lodged complaint.
On the basis of complaint, he has registered FIR by Cr.No.419/2015 and sent FIR to the court and his Superior Officers and thereafter handed over further investigation to C.W.22/P/W.8/Krishnamurthy.
The said evidence of the witness P.W.10 has completely denied by the accused counsel.
The Police Inspector Mr.Krishnamurthy examined as P.W.8.
The said witness P.W.8 after receiving further investigation from C.W.20/P.W.10.

On 16.08.2015 went to the spot and conducted spot Mahazar in the presence of panchas and seized white colour plastic can, match box having live match sticks and little burnt petty coat and saree and prepared the Mahazar at the spot itself as per Ex.P.2.
The prosecution has got marked white colour plastic can as per M.O.1, match box having live match sticks at M.O.2 and little burnt pettycoat and saree at M.Os.3 and 4 respectively.
He has received the statement given by the deceased before C.W.19/P.W.9 and same has kept in the record.
He has identified his signatures present on the said Ex.P.3 marked at Ex.P.3(b) and 3(e).
On 16.08.2015 he has collected the family photo of the deceased and accused and also xerox copy of the ration card.
On 17.08.2015 he has received intimation/Memo from Victoria hospital about death of the deceased and same has been identified by him, hence marked at Ex.P.11.
On the same day, sent a requisition to invoke Section.306 of IPC and proceed with the investigation to the concerned court.
On the same day at 6.30 p.m, the accused was produced before him.

He has carried out arrest procedure and recorded his statement and after Byatarayanapura P.S vs Mallikarjuna on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11810785/
5
his medical examination produced before the concerned court alongwith remand application and police escort.
On 19.08.2015 he has recorded statements of CWs.9, 11 to 13.
On 28.08.2015, he has received P.M.Report as per Ex.P.6, on 04.11.2015 he has recorded statement of C.W.10 and also received tax paid receipt produced by him and kept in the record.
On 06.11.2015, as the investigation was completed and as there was material evidence present against the accused, hence submitted charge sheet.
The entire evidence of the said Investigation Officer P.W8 has completely denied by the accused counsel.

Such being the case, as already stated above the prime witnesses especially the family members of the deceased not supported the prosecution story to believe due to the continuous physical and mental harassment of the accused, and as on the date of the incident, due to the scuffle between the accused and deceased, the accused poured kerosene on the deceased, at that juncture due to anguish and continuous harassment that deceased herself set ablaze by using M.O.2.
As such it is very clear from the above discussions that the prosecution has completely failed to prove the above allegations.

As such, this court has answered the point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
16. Point No.3:

In view of answer of this court on points No.1 and 2, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 306 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused stands cancelled.

MOs.1 to 4 being worthless are ordered to be destroyed after expiry of appeal time.
